thread:
maria: Quick idea: add a 'route lock' feature that temporarily pins traffic to a legacy model but does cost reconciliation in billing. This is for cases where customers see functional regressions during v2 rollout. Thoughts? :wave:
devin: Sounds useful. Two must-haves: 1) make sure billing attributes to the executed variant; 2) provide a preview/sim mode so customers can shadow traffic first.
chris: On the billing side we can add an 'effective_version' field in the charge proto. Minimal change if router sets it. But we also need to account for embedding unit differences between v1/v2.
anya: UX: call it "Lock route" instead of pin to reduce confusion with console "pin" affordance. Show TTL dropdown (1h/24h/7d/custom). Default to 24h. Add an optional reason field to surface in audit logs.
maria: Good naming. If lock is applied, console shows a small banner: "Locked to v1 until 2025-07-01 16:00 UTC by Maria — reason: breaking change in v2" with rollback button.
devin: Implementation note: add a lightweight datastore: locks(org, route, target, mode, expires). Router consults cache and applies sticky routing. For soft locks we route 99% to target, 1% continues to new version for probes.
chris: Edge: streaming / SSE clients may hold long-lived connections. If locked mid-connection, we should not reassign existing streams. Only new requests honor the lock. Make sure KV namespaces remain compatible or we risk cache poisoning.
anya: Telemetry: emit lock.created and lock.expired events with actor and reason. Also surface a diffed cost estimate when they open the lock modal. Show expected delta in token units and dollar estimate for last 24h traffic.
maria: To protect billing, require an org-level toggle to allow locking to older versions if the version is marked deprecated. Otherwise warn strongly.
devin: Dev question: how do we handle quotas? If tenant is on v2 quotas but we lock to v1, the quota engine must compute usage using v1 unitization. I propose router writes effective_version into request metadata header: X-RW-Effective-Version. Billing and quota services read that. Fallback: if header missing, fallback to route default.
chris: Note about SDKs: some drop unknown headers. Safer to also inject a tracing tag (span tag: effective.version=v1) so downstream infra can pick it up.
anya: Ops-bot: reminder - routing-service deploy v3 scheduled at 03:00 UTC with lock table migration. Please watch deploy. :rocket:
maria: Automation idea: allow auto-lock rules triggered by console alerts. e.g., if p99 error rate for route jumps >5% after rollout, console suggests a one-click lock. We still require human confirm.
devin: Add retention policy: locks auto-unlock after TTL. Also write in audit: user, reason, prev_version, new_version, ttl. Expose in Admin API: GET /admin/locks?org=...
chris: Security: only org-admins + support can create a hard lock. Soft locks (ratio-based) allowed to devs. Also rate-limit locks per org to avoid abuse.
anya: UX microcopy: "Locking routes is an emergency mitigation that may change performance/cost. Use as a temporary measure and review rollback suggestions."
maria: Follow-ups: 1) devin + chris prototype header + trace tag changes; 2) anya mock lock modal + banner; 3) ops watch deploy and add runbook. Ops-bot: ticket RW-14077 created for route-lock feature.
devin: One more thought: provide a small histogram preview of recent seqlens and token mix to help decide whether lock will change cost much. Could compute on 1h sample.
maria: Great. Let's sync in engineering sync tomorrow. Thanks everyone. :slightly_smiling_face:
